propositions: Pandoc 3.6.1 silently corrupts Markdown when converting to Jira: escapes punctuation inside code spans, deletes HTML comments, and destroys delimiters through naive arrow substitution.
A two-phase lexer must lock code fences, four-space blocks, backtick spans, HTML comments, and noformat blocks before classification to prevent pandoc from corrupting them.

An inline-Jira classifier must distinguish unambiguous wiki markers ({{…}}, [a|b], {color:}) that settle units alone from ambiguous markers (*x*, _x_) that only settle with no CommonMark markers, to prevent re-rendering oscillation.
A post-render code-preservation check must verify every source code fragment appears verbatim in the output; if any fragment is missing or corrupted, the unit falls back to its original Markdown.

The deterministic 178-body corpus (29 code-arrow / 29 table / 120 prose) must maintain >=0.90 body ratio and >=0.95 character ratio with real pandoc 3.6.1, measured over eligible safe-unit source characters.

Missing pandoc returns identity with wiki_render_fallback event (reason=pandoc_absent); conversion or preservation failure returns the unit with conversion_failure or preservation_failure reason and never logs body content.
